source_index_convention: Zero-based Python FAMINE list indices. These are not app retrieval numbers. Other passages containing equivalent evidence also qualify.

scoring.accuracy: 1 only when all required points are satisfied with no material factual contradiction or fabricated specific. Otherwise 0. Equivalent wording is accepted; exact string matching is not used.
scoring.grounding: For retrieval-enabled answers, separately score 1 if material factual claims have appropriate citations to retrieved paragraphs that support them; otherwise 0. For a pure refusal, no citation is required. For no-retrieval answers, mark grounding not applicable.
scoring.completeness: Number of satisfied required_points divided by total required_points; diagnostic only, not binary accuracy.
scoring.errors: Record API/retrieval errors separately. Do not silently drop failed questions or call them grounded refusals. Complete or explicitly report incomplete runs before comparing accuracy.

questions.question: A country has enough food in its markets, yet many households are hungry. Why might increasing crop yields alone fail to solve this problem?
questions.reference_answer: Food availability is different from household access. Income, prices, discrimination, health, or geography can prevent access even when aggregate food supplies are sufficient. Prices rising faster than wages, savings, or assistance can make available food unaffordable.
required_points: Distinguishes food availability from household access.
Explains affordability through income or prices.
Identifies at least one additional access barrier: discrimination, health, or geography.

source_excerpts.text: Food security exists when people have reliable physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, nutritious food that meets their needs and preferences. The important mechanism is how food security changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how chronic hunger changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Chronic hunger can persist even when a country has food in aggregate because household income, prices, discrimination, health, or geography limits access.

A household can become food insecure even when markets contain food if prices rise faster than wages, savings, or assistance. The important mechanism is how high food prices changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Compare cash assistance and in-kind food assistance. What market conditions favor each, and what is one logistical limitation of in-kind assistance?
questions.reference_answer: Cash can preserve choice when goods are available and people can buy them safely at reasonable prices. In-kind food may suit supply shortages, unstable prices, or a need for specific foods. Transport and storage require time and resources.
required_points: States availability, safe purchasing, and reasonable prices as conditions for cash.
Identifies supply shortage, price instability, or specific food needs as a reason for in-kind assistance.
Names transport or storage costs/time as an in-kind limitation.

source_excerpts.text: The central idea is that in-kind food assistance may be appropriate when markets lack supplies, prices are unstable, or specific foods are needed, but transport and storage take time and resources. The important mechanism is how in-kind food changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how cash transfer changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Cash assistance can preserve choice and support local markets when goods are available and recipients can purchase them safely at reasonable prices.

questions.question: How do vouchers differ from cash transfers in recipient choice, and why might a program choose vouchers?
questions.reference_answer: Cash preserves purchasing choice under suitable market conditions. Vouchers restrict purchases to selected goods or vendors and can balance choice with nutrition, market, or accountability objectives.
required_points: Explains that vouchers restrict goods or vendors.
Contrasts that restriction with cash purchasing choice.
Names nutrition, market, or accountability objectives.

source_excerpts.text: The important mechanism is how cash transfer changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Cash assistance can preserve choice and support local markets when goods are available and recipients can purchase them safely at reasonable prices.

Vouchers restrict purchases to selected goods or vendors and can balance recipient choice with nutrition, market, or accountability objectives. The important mechanism is how voucher changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Compare anticipatory action with a humanitarian needs assessment. What does each do, and what triggers anticipatory support?
questions.reference_answer: A needs assessment examines who is affected, severity, causes, duration, and feasible assistance or market options. Anticipatory action uses forecasts and pre-agreed triggers to release support before a predictable hazard causes its worst effects.
required_points: Describes identifying affected people and their needs or feasible responses.
Identifies forecasts and pre-agreed triggers.
Explains support is released before the worst effects.

source_excerpts.text: A humanitarian food-security assessment examines who is affected, how severely, why, for how long, and what assistance or market options are feasible. The important mechanism is how needs assessment changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

For a famine-prevention knowledge base, note that anticipatory action uses forecasts and pre-agreed triggers to release support before a predictable hazard causes its worst effects. The important mechanism is how anticipatory action changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Would increasing calorie availability alone address hidden hunger? Explain using the corpus.
questions.reference_answer: No. Hidden hunger involves micronutrient deficiencies even when calorie intake is sufficient. Diet quality also involves diversity, nutrient density, safety, affordability, and cultural acceptability.
required_points: Rejects calories alone as sufficient.
Explains micronutrient deficiency despite sufficient calories.
Mentions diversity or nutrient density as an additional need.

source_excerpts.text: For a famine-prevention knowledge base, note that preventing calorie deficiency does not automatically make a diet healthy; dietary diversity, nutrient density, safety, affordability, and cultural acceptability also matter. The important mechanism is how healthy diets changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Micronutrient deficiencies are sometimes called hidden hunger because a person may consume enough calories while lacking essential vitamins or minerals. The important mechanism is how hidden hunger changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Compare biofortification with food fortification. Does biofortification replace the need for a diverse diet?
questions.reference_answer: Biofortification develops staple crops with higher levels or availability of selected nutrients. Fortification adds micronutrients to commonly consumed foods. Biofortification complements rather than replaces a diverse diet; fortification needs quality control and coverage.
required_points: Distinguishes developing nutrient-enhanced crops from adding nutrients to foods.
States that biofortification does not replace dietary diversity.
Identifies quality control, suitable food vehicles, regulation, or coverage as a fortification requirement.

source_excerpts.text: Biofortification develops staple crops with higher levels or improved availability of selected nutrients and complements rather than replaces a diverse diet. The important mechanism is how biofortification changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Research and field programs generally recognize that food fortification adds selected micronutrients to commonly consumed foods and requires suitable vehicles, quality control, regulation, and population coverage. The important mechanism is how fortification changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: A farmer has limited water and is considering rainwater harvesting or drip irrigation. Compare how they work and name two constraints for each.
questions.reference_answer: Rainwater harvesting stores runoff; constraints include capacity, water quality, evaporation, maintenance, and downstream effects. Drip irrigation delivers water close to plants; constraints include filters, pressure, clogging, energy, cost, and maintenance. The corpus does not establish a universally best option.
required_points: Distinguishes storing runoff from delivering water near plants.
Names at least two listed harvesting constraints.
Names at least two listed drip constraints.
Does not declare a universally best or locally proven choice.

source_excerpts.text: Rainwater harvesting stores runoff for later use, but capacity, water quality, evaporation, maintenance, and downstream effects determine whether a design is sustainable. The important mechanism is how rainwater harvesting changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

For a famine-prevention knowledge base, note that drip irrigation delivers water close to plants and can improve control, yet filters, pressure, clogging, energy, cost, and maintenance affect real-world performance. The important mechanism is how drip irrigation changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Why is a fixed watering calendar insufficient for irrigation scheduling, and what additional limitations apply when AI interprets irrigation data?
questions.reference_answer: Scheduling should match timing and quantity to crop demand, soil water, weather, and system capacity. AI interpretation is constrained by sensor/equipment accuracy, connectivity, crop stage, and water rights.
required_points: Mentions at least three of crop demand, soil water, weather, and system capacity.
Explains that timing/quantity should adapt rather than follow only a fixed calendar.
Names at least two of equipment accuracy, connectivity, crop stage, and water rights.

source_excerpts.text: The important mechanism is how irrigation scheduling changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Irrigation scheduling matches timing and quantity to crop demand, soil water, weather, and system capacity instead of watering by a fixed calendar alone.

The important mechanism is how precision irrigation changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. AI can help interpret sensor and forecast data for irrigation, but equipment accuracy, connectivity, crop stage, and water rights constrain the recommendation.

questions.question: Compare mulching and conservation agriculture. What do they involve, and why might neither be equally practical everywhere?
questions.reference_answer: Mulch can reduce evaporation, moderate temperature, suppress weeds, and protect soil, but materials, pests, fire, and competing uses constrain it. Conservation agriculture combines reduced disturbance, soil cover, and crop diversity; outcomes depend on equipment, residues, weeds, and local ecology.
required_points: Names at least two mulch benefits and one constraint.
Identifies reduced disturbance, soil cover, and crop diversity.
Explains a conservation-agriculture dependency such as equipment, residues, weeds, or local ecology.

source_excerpts.text: One important distinction is that mulch can reduce evaporation, moderate soil temperature, suppress weeds, and protect soil, but material availability, pests, fire, and competing uses may constrain adoption. The important mechanism is how mulching changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how conservation agriculture changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Conservation agriculture commonly combines reduced soil disturbance, soil cover, and crop diversity, with outcomes depending on equipment, residues, weeds, and local ecology.

questions.question: Compare selective breeding, marker-assisted selection, and genomic selection. How is information used in each?
questions.reference_answer: Selective breeding chooses parents with useful traits and tests descendants across generations and environments. Marker-assisted selection uses DNA regions associated with traits to select plants before every trait is visible. Genomic selection uses genome-wide markers and performance data to predict breeding value for complex traits.
required_points: Describes parental selection and descendant testing.
Connects marker-assisted selection with trait-associated DNA regions.
Connects genomic selection with genome-wide markers plus performance data and predicted breeding value.

source_excerpts.text: Selective breeding changes crop populations by choosing parents with useful traits and testing their descendants across generations and environments. The important mechanism is how selective breeding changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how marker-assisted selection changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Marker-assisted selection uses identifiable DNA regions associated with traits to help breeders choose plants before every trait is visible in the field.

Genomic selection combines genome-wide marker information with performance data to predict breeding value for complex traits. The important mechanism is how genomic selection changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: A crop tolerates drought. Does that establish that it also tolerates flooding or disease? Explain what the corpus supports.
questions.reference_answer: No. Performance under one stress does not guarantee performance under another. Breeders test drought, heat, salinity, flooding, pests, or disease separately as appropriate.
required_points: Rejects automatic transfer of stress tolerance.
Explains that performance under different stresses requires testing.

source_excerpts.text: The central idea is that breeders test tolerance to drought, heat, salinity, flooding, pests, or disease because performance under one stress does not guarantee performance under another. The important mechanism is how stress tolerance changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Why should genetic engineering not be presented as an automatic solution to food insecurity?
questions.reference_answer: Its benefits, risks, and regulation depend on the crop, trait, environment, and use. Food insecurity also involves household access and income, prices, discrimination, health, or geography, so a crop trait alone does not remove every barrier.
required_points: States that benefits/risks/regulation require crop-, trait-, environment-, or use-specific assessment.
Distinguishes agricultural production from household food access.
Names at least one non-production barrier and avoids claiming guaranteed famine prevention.

source_excerpts.text: A concise explanation is that genetic engineering can introduce or alter particular traits, but benefits, risks, and regulation must be evaluated for the specific crop, trait, environment, and use. The important mechanism is how genetic engineering changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how chronic hunger changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Chronic hunger can persist even when a country has food in aggregate because household income, prices, discrimination, health, or geography limits access.

questions.question: Compare drying grain before storage with maintaining a cold chain for perishable foods. What failure risks or requirements does the corpus identify?
questions.reference_answer: Grain needs appropriate moisture before storage because excess moisture encourages mold, heating, insects, and quality loss. Cold chains slow deterioration of perishables but require reliable energy, equipment, maintenance, packaging, transport, and temperature monitoring.
required_points: Connects grain drying to moisture management.
Names at least two grain moisture risks.
Connects cold chains to slowing perishable-food deterioration.
Names at least two cold-chain requirements.

source_excerpts.text: When discussing global hunger, it helps to know that grain must be dried to an appropriate moisture level before storage because excess moisture encourages mold, heating, insects, and quality loss. The important mechanism is how drying changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Cold chains slow deterioration of perishable foods but rely on reliable energy, suitable equipment, maintenance, packaging, transport, and temperature monitoring. The important mechanism is how cold chains changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Why might rural roads and better market information both help farmers, while still addressing different problems?
questions.reference_answer: Roads can reduce travel time and damage and connect farmers to inputs, buyers, and services. Market information supports selling decisions, but prices and demand must have comparable grades, units, dates, locations, and transaction conditions.
required_points: Explains physical transport/access benefits of roads.
Explains selling-decision benefits of price/demand information.
Names at least two comparability requirements for market information.

source_excerpts.text: This concept connects agriculture with food security: reliable rural roads can reduce travel time and damage, connect farmers with inputs and buyers, and improve access to health and humanitarian services. The important mechanism is how rural roads changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

A concise explanation is that timely price and demand information can improve selling decisions, provided grades, units, dates, locations, and transaction conditions are comparable. The important mechanism is how market information changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: A crop sells at a higher price this year. Why does that not necessarily mean the farmer earns more?
questions.reference_answer: Farmgate price is what the producer receives before later transport, processing, wholesale, and retail margins. Farm income also depends on input costs such as seed, fertilizer, fuel, labor, credit, machinery, and water. A higher price alone does not establish greater income.
required_points: Defines farmgate price as producer receipts before downstream margins.
Explains that input costs affect income.
Names at least two listed input costs and avoids equating price with profit.

source_excerpts.text: The farmgate price is what a producer receives before later transport, processing, wholesale, and retail margins are added. The important mechanism is how farmgate price changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how input costs changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Seed, fertilizer, feed, fuel, labor, credit, machinery, and water costs influence whether higher production will actually improve farm income.

questions.question: How do social safety nets and resilience programs differ in emphasis when helping households cope with food-security shocks?
questions.reference_answer: Safety nets help maintain consumption and avoid selling productive assets during shocks, especially when they expand quickly and reach excluded groups. Resilience programs protect livelihoods and reduce future risk through assets, services, insurance, ecosystem restoration, or stronger institutions.
required_points: Describes maintaining consumption and/or protecting productive assets during shocks.
Describes future-risk reduction and livelihood protection.
Names at least two resilience mechanisms or one mechanism plus a safety-net coverage/expansion requirement.

source_excerpts.text: Safety nets help households maintain consumption and avoid selling productive assets during shocks, especially when systems can expand quickly and reach excluded groups. The important mechanism is how social safety nets changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Resilience programs aim to protect livelihoods and reduce future risk through assets, services, insurance, ecosystem restoration, or stronger institutions. The important mechanism is how resilience programming changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: What can generative AI contribute to early-warning reports, and why must a useful weather service communicate more than a forecast alone?
questions.reference_answer: Generative AI can summarize weather, market, conflict, crop, and nutrition reports while retaining dates and source links. Weather services should connect forecasts to decisions and communicate uncertainty, lead time, geographic resolution, and the cost of a wrong action.
required_points: Describes synthesis across at least two listed report types.
Preserves dates and source links.
Connects forecasts to decisions and names at least two of uncertainty, lead time, resolution, and wrong-action cost.

source_excerpts.text: When discussing global hunger, it helps to know that generative AI can summarize weather, market, conflict, crop, and nutrition reports for early warning while retaining dates and source links. The important mechanism is how early-warning synthesis changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Useful agricultural weather services connect forecasts with specific decisions and communicate uncertainty, lead time, geographic resolution, and the cost of a wrong action. The important mechanism is how weather services changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Compare using generated agricultural images for model training with diagnosing crop problems from photographs. What limitations affect each?
questions.reference_answer: Generated images can provide synthetic training examples but may omit rare conditions or include unrealistic features. Diagnostic image models can flag possible crop stress or disease, but similar symptoms, poor images, and unfamiliar varieties can lead to errors.
required_points: Distinguishes training-data creation from diagnosis.
Names omitted rare conditions or unrealistic generated features.
Names at least two of similar symptoms, poor images, and unfamiliar varieties as diagnosis limitations.

source_excerpts.text: Generative models can create synthetic examples for agricultural vision systems, but generated images may omit rare conditions or reproduce unrealistic features. The important mechanism is how synthetic training data changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how crop diagnosis changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Image models can flag possible crop stress or disease from photographs, yet similar symptoms, poor images, and unfamiliar varieties can cause incorrect diagnoses.

questions.question: A project wants to translate agricultural guidance for farmers. Why are translation and a user-friendly interface alone insufficient?
questions.reference_answer: Agricultural terms, measurements, crop names, and dialects need fluent local review. Farmers and extension workers should help define the problem, test the interface, identify harms, and judge whether advice fits decisions. Farm-data use also needs consent, access/retention limits, security, and benefit sharing.
required_points: Explains local language/terminology review.
Includes farmer or extension-worker involvement beyond interface appearance.
Names at least two governance considerations such as consent, access limits, retention, security, and benefit sharing.

source_excerpts.text: Research and field programs generally recognize that language models can translate extension material into more languages, but agricultural terms, measurements, crop names, and dialects require review by fluent local users. The important mechanism is how translation changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

Agricultural AI is more useful when farmers and extension workers help define the problem, test the interface, identify harms, and judge whether advice fits real decisions. The important mechanism is how human-centered design changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

The important mechanism is how data governance changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk. Farm data may reveal location, income, land use, or production, so consent, access limits, retention rules, security, and benefit sharing should be designed before collection.

questions.question: How can retrieval help reduce plausible but false agricultural advice, and what safeguards remain necessary?
questions.reference_answer: RAG uses a selected knowledge base and can show supporting documents. The corpus identifies citations, constrained outputs, expert review, and refusal as safeguards against plausible false advice. Retrieval does not establish that every generated claim is correct.
required_points: Explains retrieval of supporting knowledge and traceable evidence.
Names at least two of citations, constrained outputs, expert review, and refusal.
Does not claim retrieval guarantees correctness.

source_excerpts.text: Retrieval-augmented generation can answer agricultural questions using a selected knowledge base and can show which document supports each response. The important mechanism is how RAG advisory changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

This concept connects agriculture with food security: a language model may produce plausible but false agronomic advice, making retrieval, citations, constrained outputs, expert review, and refusal behavior important safeguards. The important mechanism is how hallucination control changes food availability, household access, diet quality, livelihood stability, or exposure to risk.

questions.question: Which exact maize variety should a farmer in the village of Kijani plant next month, and what yield in tonnes per hectare will it produce?
questions.reference_answer: The corpus does not supply village-specific conditions, a validated variety recommendation, or a numerical yield forecast. It cannot determine the requested variety and yield. General crop principles may be explained only with this limitation explicit.
required_points: Explicitly states insufficient local evidence.
Does not invent a variety or numerical yield.

questions.question: According to the corpus, what was the exact number of food-insecure residents in Indianapolis on November 1, 2026?
questions.reference_answer: The corpus does not provide that location- and date-specific statistic. The chatbot should say it cannot determine the number from the corpus.
required_points: States the requested statistic is unavailable in the corpus.
Does not invent a count or imply access to live data.

questions.question: What exact cash-transfer amount in Kenyan shillings should each household in Kijani receive next month?
questions.reference_answer: The corpus describes conditions for cash assistance but does not supply local prices, household needs, program rules, or a transfer calculation for Kijani. No exact amount can be established.
required_points: Acknowledges missing local evidence for setting the amount.
Does not supply an invented transfer amount.

questions.question: By what exact percentage did the generative-AI breeding trial described in this corpus increase drought-resistant maize yields?
questions.reference_answer: The question assumes a trial and result that the corpus does not document. It does not provide a percentage yield increase for such a trial; the chatbot should correct the premise and refuse to invent a result.
required_points: Identifies that the assumed trial/result is not documented.
Does not invent a trial, percentage, or supporting citation.

history.content: Compare cash assistance and in-kind food assistance.
Cash requires suitable markets; food assistance may suit supply shortages.
